## The problem from your seat {#your-seat}

<span class="kicker">For CPAs, enrolled agents and bookkeepers</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card card--clay"><strong>Books arrive open</strong>Clients run on Stripe, spreadsheets and you. Every month starts with matching payouts to charges and chasing the client by email.</div>
<div class="card card--clay"><strong>No proof of what didn't change</strong>When a number is questioned, you can show today's books, not that last month's books are the same books you reviewed.</div>
<div class="card card--clay"><strong>Software that taxes your seat</strong>QuickBooks caps users at every tier, so adding the accountant can force the client up a plan. QuickBooks, Xero and FreshBooks all raised prices in 2026.</div>
</div>

<p class="fine">What you care about, in our reading: clean reconciliation to Stripe; exports to QuickBooks, Xero, hledger and CSV; an audit trail; fewer client emails; recurring revenue.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/brand/trifold-brand-and-messaging.md`, "Ideal customer profiles", 4 (bookkeeper or CPA partner: serves 10–100 small businesses; cares about clean reconciliation to Stripe, exports to QuickBooks, Xero, hledger and CSV, an audit trail, fewer client emails, recurring revenue); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §2 (manual close; books changed quietly); `docs/business/market-research.md` §2 and §3 points 1–2 (price rises in 2026; QuickBooks user caps 1 / 3 / 5 / 25, "a school that adds its CPA or a second admin has to upgrade").
:::

## Provable books: what you can check {#provable-books}

<span class="kicker">Review</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--green"><strong><span class="tag tag--built">Built</span> In tfd today</strong>
<ul>
<li>Every number traces to an event; balances replay from the events and must come out the same</li>
<li>Postings balance to zero in each currency, or the event is refused</li>
<li>Reconciliation against Stripe on request (<code>tfd reconcile</code>)</li>
<li>Journals hledger reads; exports to hledger and CSV</li>
<li>Signed receipts and chained month seals, checked with <code>tfd verify</code></li>
</ul></div>
<div class="card card--ink"><strong><span class="tag tag--next">Next</span> With the hosted service</strong>
<ul>
<li>Free firm seats on every client's books, read-only or with roles</li>
<li>Managed QuickBooks and Xero sync</li>
<li>Scheduled monthly close and a CPA package</li>
<li>Daily Stripe matching, and a hash chain over every event</li>
<li>The auditor portal, with the Witnessed plan</li>
</ul></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/brand/trifold-brand-and-messaging.md`, "What exists and what is to build" (replay, `src/ledger/replay.ts`; balance check, `src/ledger/validate.ts`; hledger-readable journals; a 2026-11-07 status note on each step) and ICP 4 ("Proof": a year-end package, every number traced to an event, a read-only partner seat, `tfd verify`); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §3 (reconciliation on demand, `tfd reconcile`, released; daily matching milestone 3 and the per-event chain milestone 2 not built); `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §6 (features by tier: CSV and hledger export in Community; managed QuickBooks/Xero sync in Starter and Pro; scheduled close and CPA package in Pro; auditor role in Witnessed) and §4c (firm seats free and unlimited). Hosted service not built.

## The firm program: Trifold for Firms {#firm-program}

<span class="kicker">Tiers by active paying clients · proposed</span>

| Tier | Unlocked at | Firm pays | What it gets |
|-------|--------|--------------|---------------------|
| Listed | 1 active client | $0 | Free firm seats on every client's books; clients get 20% off their first year; a directory listing. Clients pay Trifold directly |
| Practice | 5 active clients | $99 a month, plus 30% off each client's plan | One firm bill, a dashboard across clients, books templates, Rifo closing months in a batch |
| Practice Pro | 15 active clients, or pay to unlock | $399 a month, plus wholesale per client (for example Pro $49, Witnessed $99) | Your own prices and checkout, a branded portal, credit re-billing with your markup, a white-label verify page (badge kept) |

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> Every tier, threshold and price is an assumption to test with design partners. Nothing in the program is built yet: firm accounts come first, then wholesale billing, templates, Connect checkout and the white-label portal.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §2, "Firm tiers" (verbatim prices and thresholds), "What carries over from GoHighLevel" (the program is modelled on GoHighLevel's agency model; firms resell hosted Trifold) and "Build order". Header: "Every price and rate here is an assumption... Nothing in this doc is built." The 20% first-year client discount is a placeholder (`docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §11 item 5).
:::

## What you earn: your own markup {#what-you-earn}

<span class="kicker">Economics · illustrative</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><strong>No referral fees</strong>Trifold pays accountants no cash and no referral fees. You earn from your own markup on service plus software, the way your practice already works.</div>
<div class="card card--green"><strong>An example firm</strong>30 schools on Practice Pro, each paying the firm $300 a month for bookkeeping plus software. The firm keeps about <span class="num">$7,000</span> a month for its labor; Trifold earns about <span class="num">$2,050</span> (30 × ~$55 wholesale + $399).</div>
<div class="card card--ink"><strong>White label stops at the proof</strong>You brand the portal and dashboards. Every receipt keeps its "Verify at trifold…" link, and every witnessed record keeps "Witnessed by Trifold".</div>
</div>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> The example uses draft wholesale prices (mostly Pro at $49, a few Witnessed at $99) and an assumed $300 firm fee. It illustrates the shape, not a quote.</p>

<p class="fine">Your clients own their books, and export is never paywalled, so a client can move between firms, or to Trifold directly, with its ledger intact.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §2 ("Example": 30 schools on Practice Pro at $300/mo; average wholesale about $55; Trifold ≈ $2,050/mo; the firm keeps ≈ $7,000/mo; "White label stops at the proof"), §3.3 (accountants get no cash; "the firm earns from its own markup, not from a fee Trifold pays") and §5 (a departing firm: the school owns its books, export never paywalled). No-referral-fee policy: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §4c. "Witnessed by Trifold" only on records with a valid Trifold witness signature (`TRADEMARKS.md`); the witness is not built.

Arithmetic: 30 × $55 = $1,650 + $399 = $2,049. The firm's ≈ $7,000 is the plan's figure (30 × $300 = $9,000 billed, less ~$2,050 to Trifold ≈ $6,950).
:::

## You stay the professional {#professional}

<span class="kicker">AI, data and support</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card card--green"><strong>"Will AI replace me?" No.</strong>Rifo will draft and you approve; the engine does the math. Approval modes: Off, Ask first (the default), or Auto within limits. <span class="tag tag--next">Next</span></div>
<div class="card"><strong>Vetted firms only</strong>Firms are vetted on CPA, enrolled-agent or bookkeeper credentials, under binding terms with no income claims.</div>
<div class="card card--ink"><strong>Student data</strong>A data agreement per firm; a firm sees only the roles the school grants. You handle first-line support, and Trifold supports you.</div>
</div>

<p class="fine">Trifold prepares the books and never signs or files returns. Filing stays with licensed CPAs and enrolled agents.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/brand/trifold-brand-and-messaging.md`, ICP 4 ("Objection and answer: Will AI replace me? No. The agent prepares and you sign"); `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §6 (Rifo approval modes: Off, Ask first (default), Auto within limits; "Rifo drafts, you approve, the engine does the math"); `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §5 (vetting on credentials; a data agreement per firm; first-line support by the firm); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §10 (tax preparation is regulated: Trifold prepares the books, never signs returns). Rifo is not built (AGENTS.md "Claims").
:::

## Idaho and Utah: the rules on paying accountants {#idaho-utah}

<span class="kicker">Compliance</span>

| | Idaho (Code §54-218; IDAPA 24.30.01.200) | Utah (Code §58-26a-502) |
|-----------|--------------------|-------------------|
| Commission banned when the firm also does | An attest service, or a compilation a third party will use that doesn't disclose a lack of independence | An audit or review; such a compilation; an examination of prospective financial information |
| For how long | The engagement, plus the period the statements cover | Same |
| Otherwise | Allowed, with written, clear and conspicuous disclosure of the amount or its basis, before the referral | Allowed: a commission disclosed to the person referred; a referral fee to the client |
| Also | No contingent fee for preparing a tax return | Same |

<p class="fine">Trifold pays accountants no cash, a choice stricter than either state's law, so none of these disclosures is triggered and your independence stays clean. Not checked yet: enrolled agents (IRS Circular 230), other states, and the AICPA code. Not legal advice.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §4, "Paying accountants: what Idaho and Utah allow" (the table nearly verbatim; "a choice stricter than the law"; "Not checked": enrolled agents under Circular 230, states beyond Idaho and Utah (Florida's statute is stricter), AICPA Rule 1.520; a lawyer reviews the affiliate terms, disclosures and FTC wording before launch). Primary sources listed in go-to-market "Sources": Idaho Code §54-218; IDAPA 24.30.01 section 200 (dated 3-28-23); Utah Code §58-26a-502 (last amended 2008).
:::

## Hosting tfd for many clients {#firms-and-fsl}

<span class="kicker">License · open decision</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--green"><strong>Allowed today</strong>Working on a client's own tfd install. The FSL permits professional services to a licensee, and self-hosting your own books.</div>
<div class="card card--clay"><strong>Probably not, without permission</strong>One tfd that your firm runs for many clients. That substitutes for Trifold's hosted plans, so it is likely a Competing Use under the FSL.</div>
</div>

<p class="lede">The suggested path: the hosted firm program above, or a written partner agreement on request. Whether to add a grant for firms is undecided, and will be settled before the program launches.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §4c, "Firms hosting tfd for their clients: the tradeoffs" (options A–D; suggestion A now with D on request, published as the firm program; any permission lives in a separate written grant, never an edited FSL); `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §2 (self-hosting tfd for many clients remains a Competing Use; the program is option D made public); AGENTS.md "Open licensing items", 2 (decide before the accountant partner program launches).
:::
